subject: predict() creates straight lines of locations

messages.author: 2cc58add7c2fab85
messages.subject: predict() creates straight lines of locations
parts:
Dear Chris,

I am trying to predict some missing data using the predict() function. I have high resolution data (every 8 sec). The variogramms look nice. However, the predicted locations are always in a completely straight line between the last and the next original data point. Is that normal?
As I have used my existing movement data as a "template" for the prediction, I would have expected ctmm to try to adjust the predicted data to what the original data looks like.

Thank you very much for your help.

All the best!

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: predict() creates straight lines of locations
parts:
Hi Anna,

Do you have an error model for your data and did you turn it on when fitting & selecting a movement model? https://ctmm-initiative.github.io/ctmm/articles/error.html

Best,
Chris

messages.author: 2cc58add7c2fab85
messages.subject: Re: predict() creates straight lines of locations
parts:
Hi Chris,

Thank you very much for your quick reply. I work with ATLAS Data. There are various columns in the data set that might be used to make an error model (VARX, VARY, COVXY), but as that is computationally very "expensive" I just used a generic uere(mydata) <- 10 so far.

Do you think it would be different if I tried using e.g. COVXY?:

  mydata <- as.telemetry(m[[i]], keep = "COVXY") # resulting columns are: time, X, Y, COVXY, m is a movestack
  UERE <- uere.fit( mydata )
 
  SVF1   <- variogram( mydata )
  GUESS <- ctmm.guess( mydata , CTMM=ctmm(error = T), variogram=SVF1, interactive=FALSE)
  FIT   <- ctmm.select( mydata , GUESS, trace=2)

All the best :)

messages.subject: Re: predict() creates straight lines of locations
parts:
Hi Anna,

as.telemetry() now imports those columns correctly (on Github), but it doesn't know what the projection is. I didn't see a UTM zone or anything. So the data are treated as UTM zone="1 +north" by default, with a message stating that.
Best,
Chris
